data.india: India buys most of its oil from abroad, and a lot of it comes through the Gulf. Millions of Indians live and work in Gulf countries. When West Asia burns, India feels it at the petrol pump and at home.
data.lede: Israelis and Palestinians have fought over the same land since Israel was created in 1948. Gaza is a small Palestinian territory that was run by Hamas, an armed group. Iran, Israel's biggest rival in the region, backs Hamas and other groups. Here's how the latest chapter unfolded.

players.name: Israel
players.role: PM Benjamin Netanyahu. Wants Hamas gone from Gaza.

players.name: Hamas
players.role: Armed Palestinian group that ran Gaza. Led the 7 Oct 2023 attack.

players.name: Iran
players.role: Backs Hamas, Hezbollah and the Houthis. Israel's main rival.

players.name: USA
players.role: Israel's closest ally. Brokered the Gaza ceasefire.

players.name: Hezbollah
players.role: Armed group in Lebanon, backed by Iran.

players.name: Houthis
players.role: Armed group in Yemen. Attacks ships and Israel.

timeline.what: Hamas attacks southern Israel: about 1,200 killed, 251 taken hostage. Israel declares war on Hamas and invades Gaza.
Hezbollah fires rockets from Lebanon; the Houthis attack ships in the Red Sea. Israel kills top Hamas and Hezbollah leaders.
A ceasefire frees some hostages, then collapses in March.
A US-backed Gaza ceasefire starts on 10 Oct. The remaining living hostages come home.
The US and Israel strike Iran over its nuclear programme. Supreme Leader Khamenei is killed. Iran hits back at Israel, US bases and Gulf states; shipping through Hormuz freezes.
A US–Iran ceasefire comes in June, then breaks down in July. The US blockades Iran's ports.
US–Iran talks are stalled and attacks on ships near Hormuz have surged. Tankers with Indian crews were hit on 9, 11 and 16 Oct, and a UN plan to let fertiliser ships through is stuck.

data.title: West Asia from zero

data.lede: Inflation means prices going up. A little is normal. Too much hurts everyone, especially people with less money. In India, the RBI (Reserve Bank of India) is the referee.

players.name: RBI
players.role: India's central bank. Sets the repo rate.

players.name: MPC
players.role: A 6-member committee inside RBI that votes on rates.

players.name: Government
players.role: Controls taxes, fuel duties and food stocks.

players.name: Banks
players.role: Borrow from RBI, lend to you.

timeline.what: A law gives RBI a clear job: keep inflation near 4%, within a 2–6% range.
The repo rate reaches 6.50% after a series of hikes to fight high inflation.
With prices calmer, RBI cuts rates by 1.25 points in total, down to 5.25%.
Inflation hits 4.82%, above the 4% target for the 3rd month in a row.

RBI hikes to 5.50% and September inflation hits 5.54%. Banks pass it on: SBI raises its repo-linked loan rate to 7.75% from 15 Oct, so many EMIs rise. The rupee recovers to about 94.9 per dollar after RBI sells dollars.

data.title: How RBI fights rising prices

data.lede: Every state sends MPs to the Lok Sabha based on its population. But seat counts have been frozen on the 1971 census for decades, so fast-growing states have fewer seats than their population suggests. In 2023, Parliament promised women a third of seats, but only after a new census and redrawing of seats, called delimitation. The fight now is over when and how to do both.

players.name: Union government
players.role: Wants to redraw seats and start the women's quota before 2029.

players.name: Opposition parties
players.role: Want the women's quota now, without linking it to new seat maps.

players.name: Southern states
players.role: Fear losing clout because they slowed population growth.

players.name: Delimitation Commission
players.role: A panel led by a Supreme Court judge that redraws constituencies.

players.name: Parliament
players.role: Needs a two-thirds vote to change the Constitution.

timeline.what: Seat counts per state are frozen on the 1971 census, to avoid punishing states that control population.
The last Delimitation Commission redraws constituency borders but keeps each state's seat count the same.
Parliament passes the women's reservation law: one-third of Lok Sabha and Assembly seats, but only after the next census and delimitation.
Bills to raise the seat cap to 850 and start the quota sooner win 298 votes to 230, short of the two-thirds needed.
Reports say the Centre may call a special session late this month to try again. No dates are announced yet.

data.title: Seats, maps and the women's quota

data.india: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa borders Afghanistan. Instability in a nuclear-armed neighbour matters for security across the region, including India.
data.lede: Imran Khan, a former cricket captain, became Pakistan's prime minister in 2018. He was voted out in 2022 and has been in jail since 2023. His party, PTI, says he is being targeted for political reasons; the government says he faces genuine criminal cases. The clash has spilled onto the streets again and again.

players.name: Imran Khan
players.role: Former PM and PTI founder. In jail since 2023.

players.name: PTI
players.role: Khan's party. Ran the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province until the emergency.

players.name: Federal government
players.role: Runs Pakistan from Islamabad. Says it is fighting rising terrorism.

players.name: President Asif Ali Zardari
players.role: Signed the emergency order for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

players.name: Sohail Afridi
players.role: PTI chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. PTI says he was detained.

timeline.what: Imran Khan becomes prime minister.
He loses a no-confidence vote in Parliament and is removed from office.
Khan is jailed after a corruption conviction. More cases follow.
In national elections, PTI-backed independents win the most seats, but rival parties form the government.
PTI's Sohail Afridi becomes chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Talks fail on 4 Oct and PTI starts a long march for Khan's release. On 11 Oct the president puts Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under emergency rule, and Parliament approves it on 14 Oct amid opposition walkouts.

data.title: Pakistan's Imran Khan fight

data.lede: To vote in India, your name must be on the electoral roll (voter list) for your area. The Election Commission updates these lists so names of people who died, moved or are listed twice come off, and new voters get on. SIR (Special Intensive Revision) is a deep, door-to-door re-check of those lists.

players.name: Election Commission
players.role: Runs elections and keeps voter lists. Headed by CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

players.name: INDIA bloc
players.role: Alliance of opposition parties, incl. Congress. Says SIR is unfair.

players.name: Supreme Court
players.role: Hearing challenges. On 5 Oct, refused an interim order against the CEC.

players.name: You
players.role: Any citizen 18+ can register and check their name.

timeline.what: The Supreme Court rules a voter can't be removed without notice and a hearing.
The EC runs SIR across states. Al Jazeera reports 130M+ names removed so far; millions have appealed.

Protests against SIR and the CEC run for days in Delhi after Jantar Mantar is dropped as a protest site. On 15 Oct the EC announces a lighter update (SSR) in 17 states to enrol young voters. On 17 Oct, The Hindu called the update a 'necessary corrective' but said wrongly deleted voters must be put back.

data.title: Voter lists 101: what's SIR?

data.india: Indians get most H-1B visas, and Indian IT companies are among the biggest sponsors. Every new rule hits Indian students and techies first.
data.lede: Lakhs of Indians study and work in the US. Most work there on an H-1B visa, and many hope to get a green card, which lets you live there permanently. The current US government says these routes let companies hire cheaper foreign workers instead of Americans, so it keeps adding fees and limits.

players.name: US government
players.role: Trump administration. Says it is protecting American jobs.

players.name: Tech and IT firms
players.role: Microsoft, Infosys, TCS and others that hire foreign workers.

players.name: Indian workers and students
players.role: Get nearly three-quarters of H-1B approvals.

players.name: US courts
players.role: Have blocked some new rules, like the $100,000 H-1B fee.

players.name: Government of India
players.role: Says talent mobility helps both countries.

timeline.what: Trump tries to raise the H-1B visa fee to $100,000.
A federal judge strikes down the $100,000 fee.
The US proposes a new H-1B fee of $103,265. It isn't final yet.
A White House order tells agencies to protect American workers from H-1B abuse.
The US proposes a $70,000 fee for each international student who works in the US after graduating (OPT).
The US freezes the green card route (PERM) at eight firms, including Microsoft, Infosys, TCS, Wipro and HCL.

data.title: America's work-visa squeeze

data.india: Russia is now India's biggest source of crude oil. The Black Sea route carries grain and sunflower oil, and five Indian sailors have died in attacks on ships there this year.
data.lede: Ukraine was part of the Soviet Union until 1991, then became independent. Russia sees Ukraine as part of its sphere and opposes its move towards the West. In 2014 Russia took Crimea, and in 2022 it launched a full invasion. Now both sides also attack each other's power plants, refineries and Black Sea shipping.

players.name: Russia
players.role: President Vladimir Putin. Invaded Ukraine in 2022.

players.name: Ukraine
players.role: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Fighting to defend its land.

players.name: USA
players.role: President Trump. Pushing for a deal; eased curbs on Russian diesel.

players.name: Europe
players.role: Backs Ukraine with money and weapons.

players.name: India
players.role: Buys Russian oil. Proposed a 3-part truce on energy and shipping.

timeline.what: Russia takes Crimea from Ukraine. Fighting starts in eastern Ukraine.
Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Fighting has gone on ever since.
India sends Kyiv and Moscow a 3-part plan: no attacks on energy sites, free Black Sea trade, safe ships.
The US lets Russian diesel back into world markets to ease a global fuel shortage. Zelenskyy calls it a gift to Putin.
Trump announces an energy ceasefire. Zelenskyy says Ukraine wasn't told and Russian strikes continued.

data.title: Russia–Ukraine war, simply
